summary:
A hard first Christmas after a loss is often part of typical grief. Research shows distress can rise around meaningful dates in the early months after a loss. Prolonged grief is different: longing that stays intense for many months and makes daily life hard to manage.

Our new article from psychologist Matthew Hallam explains the difference, and when it may be worth talking to your GP.

Equal Psychology provides psychological support for adults experiencing grief and loss in Kew, Croydon, and online across Melbourne.

Medicare rebates available with a GP referral.

Read more: https://www.equalpsychology.com.au/post/grief-at-christmas-prolonged-grief
